note: validateWill(d) returns only { validityClass, formalityRisk, sharesTotalPercent, witnessCount } (no rules array, no flags), so this is a SPLIT engine: the oracle pins detectFlaggedIssues(state) as expected.flaggedIssues with flagsArgs ["state"], mirroring form-app.js. Classification is first-match: formalityRisk (testator under 18, capacity denied, domicile outside England and Wales, marriage expected without a contemplation clause, witness under 18, witness is a beneficiary by answer or by name, signed with fewer than two witnesses, signed with an execution answer not yes) -> formality-risk; else incomplete (name or date of birth missing, capacity or voluntariness not yes, no executor, no beneficiary, residuary clause not yes, shares not totalling 100, minor beneficiary without trustee) -> incomplete; else valid. The testator age is measured at dateOfWill if set, else at the frozen wall clock. Flags are stable-sorted high > medium > low. The timestamp key is added by form-app.js. Regenerate expected with: bin/test-personas united-kingdom-last-will-and-testament --update

personas.name: Valid draft, ready to execute
personas.description: A widowed 68-year-old in England and Wales leaves her estate (under £325,000) equally to her two adult children, with two executors, a residuary clause, a cremation wish, and Inheritance Act claims considered. Still a draft with no witnesses named yet. Expect validityClass valid, no formality risk, shares 100, and only the low reminder that witnesses are not yet arranged.

estate.specificGiftsNotes: My wedding ring to my daughter Anna.

flaggedIssues.description: Two independent adult witnesses are not yet named. They must both watch the testator sign and then sign themselves.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Arrange two adult witnesses who are not beneficiaries or married to a beneficiary.

personas.name: Valid and signed with two independent witnesses
personas.description: The same will after execution on 2026-08-20: written, signed, two adult witnesses present together who each signed, neither a beneficiary. Expect validityClass valid, two witnesses and no flags.

personas.name: Blank will record
personas.description: Nothing answered. Expect validityClass incomplete: the testator details, capacity, executor, beneficiaries and residuary clause are all missing, and the engine raises the matching high and medium flags.

flaggedIssues.description: No executor is named. Executors collect the estate, pay debts and tax, and distribute the gifts.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Appoint at least one executor, ideally two, and a professional or a replacement if they may not outlive you.

flaggedIssues.description: No beneficiary is named, so the will does not say who inherits.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Name each beneficiary and the share of the residuary estate they receive.

flaggedIssues.description: The will does not confirm a residuary clause. Anything not specifically given away (the residuary estate) passes under the intestacy rules instead.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Add a residuary clause that gives everything not otherwise left to named beneficiaries, with a fallback if one dies first.

flaggedIssues.description: Capacity and voluntariness are not both confirmed as yes.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Confirm that the testator understands what a will does, the extent of the estate, and who might expect to inherit, and is acting freely.

flaggedIssues.description: The testator name or date of birth is missing.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Record the testator’s full legal name and date of birth.

flaggedIssues.description: It is not confirmed that claims under the Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Act 1975 were considered. A spouse or civil partner, a former partner, a partner of two years or more, a child, a child of the family, or anyone financially maintained may apply to court within six months of the grant of probate if the will leaves them without reasonable provision.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: List who might claim, provide for them, or record the reason for leaving them out in a signed letter kept with the will.

flaggedIssues.description: Two independent adult witnesses are not yet named. They must both watch the testator sign and then sign themselves.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Arrange two adult witnesses who are not beneficiaries or married to a beneficiary.

flaggedIssues.description: Funeral wishes are not recorded. They are not legally binding on the executors, but they guide them.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Record burial or cremation and any wishes, and tell the executors.

personas.name: Shares total 80% and a minor beneficiary with no trustee
personas.description: Two adult children each receive 40% and a nine-year-old grandchild is named with a 0% share and no trustee, so the shares total 80% and no trustee holds the child's share. Expect validityClass incomplete with the shares-not-100 and minor-beneficiary-no-trustee flags.

estate.specificGiftsNotes: My wedding ring to my daughter Anna.

flaggedIssues.description: The beneficiary shares total 80%, not 100%. A residuary estate that is over- or under-allocated causes disputes and partial intestacy.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Adjust the percentage shares so they total exactly 100%.

flaggedIssues.description: A beneficiary is under 18 and no trustee is appointed. A child cannot give a valid receipt for an inheritance, and the share would have no one to manage it.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Appoint trustees to hold the share until the child reaches the age you choose (often 18, or later).

flaggedIssues.description: Two independent adult witnesses are not yet named. They must both watch the testator sign and then sign themselves.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Arrange two adult witnesses who are not beneficiaries or married to a beneficiary.

personas.name: Signed with only one witness
personas.description: Recorded as signed and witnessed, but only one witness is named. Expect validityClass formality-risk, a high fewer-than-two-witnesses flag, and witnessCount 1.

estate.specificGiftsNotes: My wedding ring to my daughter Anna.

flaggedIssues.description: The will is recorded as signed but only 1 witness is named. A will must be signed or acknowledged by the testator in the presence of at least two witnesses present at the same time (Wills Act 1837 s.9).
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Name both witnesses. If the will was signed with fewer than two, it is unlikely to be valid; sign a fresh will correctly.

personas.name: Witness is also a beneficiary
personas.description: The first witness, Anna Ellis, is the daughter who receives 50% of the estate. Expect validityClass formality-risk with the witness-is-beneficiary flag, because her gift would fail under Wills Act 1837 s.15.

estate.specificGiftsNotes: My wedding ring to my daughter Anna.

flaggedIssues.description: A witness, or the spouse or civil partner of a witness, is a beneficiary. The will stays valid but that gift fails (Wills Act 1837 s.15). GOV.UK: you cannot leave your witnesses, or their married partners, anything in your will.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Choose two independent adult witnesses who are not beneficiaries or married to one.

personas.name: Testator aged 17
personas.description: A 17-year-old drafts a will. Expect validityClass formality-risk and the testator-under-18 flag, since the testator must be 18 or over.

estate.specificGiftsNotes: My wedding ring to my daughter Anna.

flaggedIssues.description: The testator is under 18. Only a person aged 18 or over can make a valid will (Wills Act 1837 s.7), apart from a few narrow exceptions such as some members of the armed forces on active service.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Do not sign. Wait until the testator is 18, or take legal advice about whether an exception applies.

flaggedIssues.description: Two independent adult witnesses are not yet named. They must both watch the testator sign and then sign themselves.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Arrange two adult witnesses who are not beneficiaries or married to a beneficiary.

personas.name: Marriage expected without a contemplation clause
personas.description: The testator is engaged and the will does not say it is made in contemplation of the marriage, so the marriage would revoke it. Expect validityClass formality-risk and the marriage-revocation flag.

estate.specificGiftsNotes: My wedding ring to my daughter Anna.

flaggedIssues.description: A marriage or civil partnership is expected. Marrying or forming a civil partnership revokes an earlier will unless it was made in expectation of that marriage and says so (Wills Act 1837 s.18).
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Add a clause stating the will is made in contemplation of the named marriage or civil partnership, or plan to make a new will after the ceremony.

flaggedIssues.description: Two independent adult witnesses are not yet named. They must both watch the testator sign and then sign themselves.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Arrange two adult witnesses who are not beneficiaries or married to a beneficiary.

flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Take advice from a solicitor in the relevant jurisdiction.

flaggedIssues.description: The record says the testator lacks testamentary capacity or is not making the will freely. A will made without capacity, or under undue influence, can be set aside.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Take legal advice before going further. Where capacity is in doubt, a medical assessment at the time of signing is good practice.

flaggedIssues.description: Two independent adult witnesses are not yet named. They must both watch the testator sign and then sign themselves.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Arrange two adult witnesses who are not beneficiaries or married to a beneficiary.

personas.name: Valid but complex: partner, children, foreign property, large estate
personas.description: A cohabiting testator with children under 18, no guardian, a property in Spain, an earlier will not revoked, an estate over £2 million, and Inheritance Act claims not yet considered; the content is complete (executor, shares 100%). Expect validityClass valid with a cluster of medium and low awareness flags: partner not provided for, other jurisdictions, previous will, guardian not named, Inheritance Act, inheritance tax.

estate.specificGiftsNotes: My wedding ring to my daughter Anna.

flaggedIssues.description: The testator lives with an unmarried partner who is not named as a beneficiary. An unmarried partner inherits nothing under the intestacy rules, and may have to claim under the Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Act 1975.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Decide whether to provide for the partner in the will, and say so explicitly.

flaggedIssues.description: The estate includes property outside England and Wales. Foreign property is often governed by local succession law, and a separate will may be needed there.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Take advice on whether a separate will, or local formalities, are needed for that property.

flaggedIssues.description: An earlier will exists and this will does not expressly revoke it. Two wills can conflict.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Add a clause revoking all earlier wills and codicils, and destroy or file the old will as advised.

flaggedIssues.description: The testator has children under 18 but no guardian is named. A will can name who should look after them if no parent with parental responsibility survives.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Name a guardian (and a reserve), and talk to them first.

flaggedIssues.description: It is not confirmed that claims under the Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Act 1975 were considered. A spouse or civil partner, a former partner, a partner of two years or more, a child, a child of the family, or anyone financially maintained may apply to court within six months of the grant of probate if the will leaves them without reasonable provision.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: List who might claim, provide for them, or record the reason for leaving them out in a signed letter kept with the will.

flaggedIssues.description: Two independent adult witnesses are not yet named. They must both watch the testator sign and then sign themselves.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Arrange two adult witnesses who are not beneficiaries or married to a beneficiary.

flaggedIssues.description: It is not confirmed that every executor is an adult who is willing to act.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Ask each executor to agree, and confirm they are 18 or over.

flaggedIssues.description: The estate may exceed the £325,000 inheritance tax nil-rate band. Anything left to a spouse, civil partner or charity is normally exempt. Leaving the home to children or grandchildren can add a residence nil-rate band of up to £175,000 (tapered for estates above £2 million). Leaving at least 10% of the net estate to charity can lower the rate to 36%.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Consider tax planning, and take advice if the estate is large or complex.

flaggedIssues.description: Funeral wishes are not recorded. They are not legally binding on the executors, but they guide them.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Record burial or cremation and any wishes, and tell the executors.
